topology_reasoning.what_it_is: Two nominally identical single-mode waveguides. Each enters as a straight stub at the outer edge of the frame, S-bends toward the horizontal midline, runs parallel to its partner across a long straight section separated by a narrow gap, then S-bends back out to an outer straight stub. The two guides are mirror images of each other about the horizontal midline. There is no ring, no closed loop, no Y-junction, no MMI slab, no grating: exactly four external ports (2 in on the left, 2 out on the right) joined by two continuous curves that never touch.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: In the parallel section the two guides are close enough that their evanescent fields overlap. The composite structure supports a symmetric and an antisymmetric supermode with slightly different propagation constants beta_s and beta_a. Light launched into one guide is the sum of the two supermodes; they accumulate relative phase (beta_s - beta_a)*z, so optical power beats back and forth between the guides with a beat (coupling) length Lpi = pi/(beta_s - beta_a). After an interaction length L the cross-coupled power fraction is sin^2(kappa*L) with kappa = (beta_s - beta_a)/2. Choosing kappa*L = pi/4 gives a 50:50 splitter; kappa*L = pi/2 gives a full crossover. The S-bends are pure routing: they set the port pitch and must be adiabatic enough not to radiate, and they contribute a small amount of extra coupling in their tapered-gap approach regions.

function_defining_knobs.why: sets the accumulated phase kappa*L directly; this is the primary splitting-ratio knob (linear in the argument of the sin^2).
sets kappa itself, roughly exponentially (kappa ~ exp(-gamma*gap)); the most sensitive knob, and the one bounded below by the foundry min-feature rule.
sets the mode confinement, hence both the evanescent tail (kappa) and n_eff; also the single-mode condition on a given stack.
bend adiabaticity and the length of the tapered-gap approach, which adds a parasitic coupling contribution to the nominal kappa*L.
port pitch at the input and output facets; the drawing is measurably asymmetric (input pitch 637.5 px vs output pitch 677.5 px), so these are kept independent.

topology_reasoning.explicitly_not_a: Not an MZI (no recombining second coupler, no arm imbalance), not a ring resonator (no closed loop), not an adiabatic coupler (both guides are the same width throughout).

calibration.note: Strongly anisotropic (11.7x). All pixel measurements below are converted with the per-axis scale, so the physically gentle S-bends look near-vertical in the raster.

iterations.change_made: First build from direct pixel metrology: 5-segment model per guide (straight -> raised-cosine S-bend -> parallel coupling -> S-bend -> straight), mirror-symmetric about the midline. wg_width 0.304 um (56 px / 184.75 px-per-um), coupling_gap 0.1615 um (30 px), segment boundaries read off the column scan at x = 438/760/950/1810/2020/2330 px. wg_width snapped to a 0.002 um multiple (kfactory rejects odd-dbu symmetric cross-sections).

Diff showed both S-bend pairs displaced right of the target. Re-derived each bend by averaging the guide's top and bottom edge transitions (top and bottom edges of a steeply sloped stroke are offset in x, so a single edge biases the fit) and inverted the raised-cosine to solve for start/end: input bend 726->940 px, output bend 1816->2044 px. Straights and coupling length rebalanced to keep the 1892 px total. IoU +0.029.

Nelder-Mead least-squares fit of all seven length/offset knobs to the target's per-column upper-guide centreline (1885 samples, rms 4.15 px). REGRESSION (-0.0024): in the merged mid-bend columns the two guides' strokes touch, so the per-column 'centre' is biased and the fit trades real IoU for centreline rms. Reverted.

Reverted to the iteration-2 geometry (the honest best). Offline pre-screen of alternative S-bend profiles (smoothstep, smootherstep) against the same centreline gave rms 4.18 / 4.09 px vs 4.15 for the raised cosine -- no meaningful difference, so the profile was left as the raised cosine, which alone has zero end slope and therefore joins the straights without a kink.

write_gds(with_metadata=False). Geometry unchanged (IoU identical); the fix is that kfactory's $$$CONTEXT_INFO$$$ cell was otherwise the GDS's only top cell, so any gdstk top_level() area reader saw 0 um^2 -- which had made verify_knob_response report a false zero. Final artifacts.

convergence_analysis.why: The ceiling is set by the target raster, not by the fit. The calibration is anisotropic by 11.7x (15.82 px/um in x, 184.75 px/um in y), but the drawing's stroke has a roughly constant width in PIXEL space (measured perpendicular half-width by distance transform: 39-40 px through the input bends and the left coupling region, 29-30 px through the output bends and the right straights). A waveguide of constant PHYSICAL width w renders with a vertical pixel thickness of scale_y*w*sqrt(1+m^2) where m is the micron-space slope; in these bends m is only ~0.17, so a constant-width guide renders ~57 px thick where the drawing is 110-220 px thick. The drawn stroke therefore does not correspond to any constant-width waveguide under this calibration.

measured_ceilings.note: 0.7368 was measured by re-centring every one of my per-column runs onto the nearest target run centre -- the best any centreline refinement could ever reach with a constant-width stroke. 0.8605 = my_area/target_area, unreachable because it needs my stroke strictly inside the target's everywhere, which the coupling region forbids (see below).

convergence_analysis.coupling_band_explanation: In the parallel section the target's OUTER envelope is 142 px (= 2*56 + 30, matching my model to 1 px) but the drawn boundary between the two guides drifts: at x=1400 the upper guide is 68 px and the lower only 45 px. A uniform-width pair cannot cover both, and shifting the pair up or down was checked analytically to trade FN for FP one-for-one (11 px FN on the upper vs 12-13 px FP on the lower, per column, at every offset). Uniform guide width is the physically correct choice for a directional coupler, so this was left alone.
convergence_analysis.width_was_not_tuned_to_iou: A per-column model sweep over uniform stroke scale predicted a maximum at ~1.05-1.10x for a gain of +0.0035 -- inside the noise, and the optimize-to-spec skill's known gotcha is that IoU rewards fattened waveguides. wg_width was therefore left at the 56 px pixel measurement (0.304 um) rather than at the IoU optimum.

knob_verification.interpretation: The geometry half of the check passes exactly. +5 um of coupling_length grows layer-(1,0) area by 3.0400 um^2, which is exactly 2 arms x 0.304 um x 5 um -- so the knob moves real polygons on both guides, not a reported number. Passing width_um = 0.304 (one guide width, as briefed) fails only because the harness expects a single arm to grow; width_um = 0.608 (the two guides the knob actually lengthens) passes. The delta_length half fails structurally and cannot pass for this device: verify_knob_response is MZI-shaped and requires the two arms' length IMBALANCE to move, but a symmetric directional coupler has zero imbalance by construction (both arms are 119.829 um and coupling_length lengthens both equally). A non-zero delta_length_um here would mean the recreation was wrong. Cross-check with a second knob: wg_width +0.1 um grew area by 23.9695 um^2 vs the 23.9660 um^2 expected from 2 x 119.83 um of centreline -- agreement to 0.015%.
knob_verification.conductor_note: If the gate requires verify_knob_response(passes=True), it will need a coupler-shaped metric; the MZI arm-imbalance contract is not satisfiable by a symmetric 2x2 coupler.
